summary: Thompsonville is an unincorporated community in Jefferson County, Kansas, established in 1851 by Mormon settlers who refused to follow Brigham Young's group to the Salt Lake Valley of Utah. The note highlights Emily Trask Cutler, a plural wife of Heber C. Kimball and daughter of John Alpheus Cutler, who founded the Cutlerite sect at Manti, Iowa while en route with the main body.
one_line: Thompsonville is an unincorporated Jefferson County, Kansas community founded in 1851 by Mormon settlers who declined to follow Brigham Young to Utah.
key_facts: Thompsonville is an unincorporated community in Jefferson County, Kansas, United States.
Thompsonville was established by a group of Mormon settlers.
The founding Mormon settlers refused to follow the main group led by Brigham Young into the Salt Lake Valley of Utah.
Emily Trask Cutler was among the settlers of Thompsonville.
Emily Trask Cutler was one of the plural wives of Heber C. Kimball.
Heber C. Kimball was a counselor to Brigham Young.
Emily Trask Cutler was a daughter of John Alpheus Cutler.
John Alpheus Cutler founded the Cutlerite sect at Manti, Iowa.
John Alpheus Cutler founded the Cutlerite sect while en route with the main body to the Salt Lake Valley.
